Hi Samir — looping in a few quick technical notes from the runtime/SDK perspective. High level answers to your numbered items below; happy to expand on any in the sync.

1) Auth
- OAuth2 client_credentials is a first-class flow for our hosted API and dedicated deployments. Tokens are short-lived (1h) by default; we recommend server-side rotation with a refresh token or our token-exchange endpoint. For Dedicated/Private we support mTLS for extra security — we'll include config examples in the sync.

2) Embeddings + Reranker latency
- Recommended pattern: embed queries + top-k retrieval via ANN (Faiss/HNSW) in parallel, then batch candidate rerank calls using a compact prompt per candidate (avoid resending large context).
- Use our batching library that packs multiple candidate scoring calls into a single model request (we support dynamic batching up to N candidates per request). That typically gets reranker p95 under 350–450ms for k=50 on dedicated GPU pools if you set batch size appropriately.

3) Chat vs Completions & structured output
- For structured outputs and tool-calling we recommend the chat endpoint with function-calling (aka tool-calling). It provides deterministic boundaries (function call token markers) and a JSON schema enforcement layer you can opt into — this is stronger than naive stop-token techniques on completions.
- Stop sequences on completions are literal token sequences and may truncate mid-JSON if not careful; function-calling returns a discrete call payload.

4) Tokenization / max_tokens
- Token count = prompt_tokens + response_tokens. Model max is fixed (e.g., 8192). We recommend: max_response_tokens = min(model_max - estimate_prompt_tokens - safety_buffer, customer_desired_limit). Our SDK includes a fast token-estimator (language-dependent) you can call locally before sending. See example in example-chat-vs-completions-requests.txt.

5) Streaming semantics
- We support chunked streaming (SSE or chunked HTTP). Partial events are sent as UTF-8 safe chunks (so incremental render is OK). For structured outputs, the recommended approach is: (a) use function-calling to receive a final structured payload, or (b) if you stream JSON, validate/reassemble on the client and fallback to fetching the final non-streamed response if the streaming session ends abruptly.

Example request notes (high-level)
- Chat + function-calling (preferred)
  POST /v1/chat/completions
  {
    "model": "rwd-chat-1",
    "messages": [...],
    "functions": [{"name":"kb_lookup", "parameters": {...}}],
    "stream": true
  }

- Completions (legacy, unstructured)
  POST /v1/completions
  {
    "model": "rwd-complete-1",
    "prompt": "...",
    "max_tokens": 256,
    "stop": ["

"]
  }
